description:
Goal
Make the shared Enum.reduce* bridge activation/return analysis converge to one fixed point across List, Range, and Map by joining surfaces and returns monotonically in the addressed-arrow frame.

Design intent
Activation inputs, CallableSurface, and source contracts are already the same addressed-arrow principle at different boundaries. The fix should use that principle: join caller evidence by addressed slot identity and own-surface suffix, not by raw positional capture prefix in a surrounding executable layout.

Required work
- Audit resolve_closure_call / callsite summary / activation input contribution paths for the bridge reducer and identify where non-List collection-state prefixes cause a captured callable to become a template, None return, or multiple boundary surfaces.
- Replace any non-monotone re-grounding/replacement of callable surfaces with a join over CallableSurface sets and return evidence; absent evidence stays None, proven empty stays none(), and concrete returns ascend by union/widening only.
- Use own_surface / own_surface_past_captures as the compatibility operation for suffix comparison; do not compare raw slots after collection-state prefixes.
- Add a regression that Range+Map reduce/to_list compiles within the normal drive budget and shows bounded activation_analysis/return_type churn.

Checks
- fz-bfh.4 no longer drive-limit storms.
- enum_tier0 with List+Range+Map reduce/2, reduce/3, reduce_while/3 reaches transport instead of oscillating.
- ReturnType widening telemetry is not used as the normal escape hatch for this cluster.

comments.text: INVESTIGATION CHECKPOINT (not yet implemented). Ground truth confirmed: f98.2's addressed-frame surface match is already correct -- runtime_demand.rs:519-522 compares own_surface (past captures) to surface.inputs and skips on mismatch, NOT a raw-slot compare. So f98.3's locus is the RETURN-EVIDENCE join, not the surface match. Per f98's pinned telemetry (~52941 activation_analysis re-derivations paired 1:1 with return_type; #1 oscillator Enum.reduce fn69; churning Map-reduce callsite with return_ty: None on Ty(19) -- same fn/type as fz-bfh.3's absent value), the storm is a NON-MONOTONE RETURN ASCENT: the shared bridge executable's return type drops back to None rather than widening monotonically once concrete evidence arrives ([[unknown-is-not-none]] / convergence-by-construction). FIX SHAPE (Output Contract Loop, fresh budget): (1) reproduce the range+map storm with the fz-bfh.7 JobBudgetGuard to name the oscillating kind loud; (2) trace to the exact site where the bridge return_ty is RE-GROUND to None instead of joined; (3) make the join widen-only -- absent stays None, proven-empty stays none(), concrete ascends by union only -- and DELETE the re-grounding (the 'remove what's no longer necessary'); (4) regression: range+map reduce/to_list compiles within the normal drive budget with bounded activation_analysis/return_type churn (guard-observed), ReturnType widening telemetry NOT the escape hatch. Did NOT implement at this session's context depth to avoid the sprawl class we just cleaned (see fz-bfh.5.5 history).

CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (ran the three deferred fixtures with defers stripped on HEAD 8a91e9c90 — ground truth, not the stale pinned telemetry the prior checkpoint relied on):

NO STORM EXISTS. The semantic drive converges. The prior 'non-monotone return-ascent storm' hypothesis does NOT reproduce: a range+map reduce/3 probe reaches semantic closure AND transport in <4k jobs, and define_return already treats None as a no-op bottom on the join path. The ~52941 figure was a pre-f98.1/.2 measurement; f98.1 (pin reduce bridge callable contract) + f98.2 (keep boundary surfaces authoritative) already settled the convergence.

Actual current state of the three regression targets:
- fz_f98_range_reduce_scalar (bfh.1, reduce/3 over Range): ALL THREE PATHS PASS. Its defer.* flags are STALE and should be removed.
- fz_f98_range_reduce2 (bfh.2, reduce/2 over stepped Range): FAILS at transport.rs:338 — 'transport shape anchors disagree for connected position component'. The shared bridge reducer FunctionId(174) input0 is anchored to BOTH ShapeId(11) and ShapeId(14) within one connected union component (equalities cite transport.rs:1423/1887/1935). A shape-anchor conflict, NOT a return-ascent oscillation.
- fz_f98_range_map_converges (bfh.4, to_list Range+Map): FAILS at native lowering — 'native callable materialization for FunctionId(174)/0 matched multiple native boundaries' (e.g. [NativeCallableBoundaryId(8),(11)] for one published BoundaryId(21)). Same root cause one layer down: the shared bridge callable resolves to MULTIPLE boundaries.

REVISED LOCUS: the live defect is the shared bridge (FunctionId(174)) carrying MULTIPLE callable shapes/boundaries at ONE published transport position — the bfh.2 'multi-surface callable value resolved by native pick-first instead of producer identity' problem, surfacing as (a) conflicting transport ShapeId anchors and (b) multiple native boundaries. The fix belongs in transport callable-boundary identity / shape anchoring, NOT in the semantic return join. Next: determine whether ShapeId(11) vs (14) are layout-identical (interning/identity fragmentation — see [[feedback_shapeid_is_pure_layout]]) or genuinely divergent layouts (bridge needs per-shape boundary identity). The prior monotone-return fix is moot and was NOT implemented (good — it would not have touched these failures).

title: Make shared reduce bridge surface and return joins monotone
